# Code Review Report

## Review Summary

This branch removes the TypeScript tool wrappers and introduces a Python console entry point with new `story-writer` subcommands. The overall direction is reasonable, but the current packaging metadata contains a release-blocking backend declaration, and two of the newly advertised CLI flags do not change runtime behavior as documented.

**Files Reviewed:** 30
**Findings:** 1 Critical, 3 Warning, 0 Suggestion

## Findings

### Critical Findings

[C-01] Invalid PEP 517 backend blocks package builds
Category: Correctness
Severity: Critical
File: pyproject.toml
Lines: 1-3
Description: The new build backend is declared as `setuptools.backends.legacy:build`, which is not a supported setuptools PEP 517 backend. Standard setuptools backends are `setuptools.build_meta` or `setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__`. With the current value, `pip install .` / wheel builds will fail before the `story-writer` console script can be generated, which defeats the purpose of this PR.
Suggestion: Switch to a supported backend, for example `build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"`, and keep the script entry point under `[project.scripts]`. If package discovery needs to be explicit, add the appropriate setuptools package configuration in the same file.

### Warning Findings

[W-01] `--batch` flag is currently a no-op
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: src/presentation/cli/main.py
Lines: 36-49
Description: `_cmd_run()` accepts `batch`, immediately discards it via `_ = batch`, and always constructs `NullApprovalGate()`. `run_pipeline()` derives `batch_mode` from `isinstance(gate, NullApprovalGate)`, so `story-writer run` behaves as batch mode even when `--batch` is omitted. The parser help text promises a mode switch that does not exist.
Suggestion: Either implement distinct non-batch behavior for `run` or remove the flag until an interactive approval gate exists. The help text should match the actual runtime behavior.

[W-02] `resume --savepoint` advertises targeted resume, but runtime always loads latest state
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: src/presentation/cli/main.py
Lines: 52-63
Description: The CLI forwards `savepoint` into `resume_pipeline()`, but the orchestrator implementation still calls `_load_savepoint(story_name)` with no savepoint selector and resumes from the single latest `pipeline_state.json`. The provided savepoint name is only checked for membership in `state.savepoints`; it does not control which savepoint is loaded. Users can therefore request a named savepoint and silently resume the wrong state.
Suggestion: Either implement real savepoint selection in `resume_pipeline()` / `_load_savepoint()` or remove the `--savepoint` option until the backend supports it.

[W-03] `tui` subcommand is exposed even though the TUI package is absent
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: src/presentation/cli/main.py
Lines: 19-33
Description: The new parser exposes `story-writer tui` as a normal subcommand, but there is no `src/presentation/tui/` package in the repository. `_cmd_tui()` therefore falls into the `ImportError` branch every time and exits with status 1. That makes the newly shipped command permanently non-functional on this branch.
Suggestion: Do not register the `tui` subcommand until the TUI module exists, or gate it behind an optional extra with documentation and tests that verify the availability check.

### Suggestions

None.

## Overall Assessment

This branch is not ready to merge as-is. The packaging metadata likely prevents installation of the new console script entirely, and the new CLI surface over-promises behavior for `--batch`, `--savepoint`, and `tui`. Once the backend declaration is corrected and the exposed command contracts are aligned with real runtime behavior, the rest of the migration looks straightforward.
